evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Jules: 'I can certainly get you an estimate right now. I just need you know additional information to get us on the right track that should take me about like ten to fifteen minutes or so and then I can get you an accurate code. Sounds good to you.' — framing present but no clear wait for affirmative response before proceeding.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Jules: 'Aside from the, you know, quote in general, do you have any other concerns about your upcoming move or anything, any important questions you want answers during this call today?' — asked before probing details.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Bret raises storage unit logistics (two-part move, 10x10 and 5x5 units down the hall). Jules responds 'Sounds good. It does. Thank you.' and then pivots to 'can you give me like the quick, a quick list of the items we're going to be moving?' — no 'tell me more' follow-up, but the concern was clarified by Bret's own elaboration. Follow-up on the storage complexity is present in the item listing that follows.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Jules acknowledges ('Sounds good') but does not reflect back the two-part move structure or confirm all concerns were captured.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Jules: 'for this move-in particular, this move could take anywhere from the minimum of two and a half to four hours at the most just in case the disassemble and would be a little bit complicated and so for this move, I would budget anywhere from $505 to $808' — range anchored to home size/complexity and personalized to the specific job (disassembly, multiple stops).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Jules covers hourly rate ($202/hr for 3 movers + truck), minimum (2.5 hrs), proration (15 min increments), deposit for moving blankets ($14, refundable), and that rate includes gas, truck, taxes, insurance, tools, wrapping. 'Does that make sense' checks follow pricing blocks. No explicit 'not a guess' framing or fee disclosure before the customer asks.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Jules moves directly to booking: 'Awesome, alright, well, I will get you scheduled right now for Sunday October 4th.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No section closing the loop. Jules skips both promises entirely and moves to booking.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Jules transitions to scheduling: 'Awesome, alright, well, I will get you scheduled right now for Sunday October 4th.'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent. Jules assumes yes and moves directly to scheduling: 'Awesome, alright, well, I will get you scheduled right now for Sunday October 4th.'
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Date (Sunday October 4th), arrival window (8:30–9 AM), and confirmation email mentioned. Missing: phone number, crew size (implied 3 movers + truck from rate, but not explicitly re-confirmed), delivery address not stated on call, notes about concerns not recorded for crew.

top_strength: Jules gathered comprehensive logistics details across both pickup and storage stops, asked the customer's agenda early before probing, and followed up on the two-part move structure to clarify a complex job without oversimplifying.
coaching_note: Skip directly from pricing into booking without asking 'Does that feel fair?' first, and skip the Two Promises section entirely — both are load-bearing parts of the call card that protect the sale and build confidence; add them back before moving to scheduling.
